item.title: Satellite data and weather models improve short-term solar irradiance forecasts in China
item.description: The intermittent nature of solar energy poses challenges to grid stability, making accurate ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting crucial for balancing supply and demand. However, traditional numerical weather prediction models often struggle with cloud initialization, leading to forecast inaccuracies.

item.title: The science of how (and when) we decide to speak out—or self-censor
item.description: The study's main takeaway: "Be bold. It is the thing that slows down authoritarian creep."

item.title: Lawsuit over Trump rejecting medical research grants is settled
item.description: Settlement forces NIH to review grants previously rejected on ideological grounds.

item.title: DOGE did not find $2T in fraud, but that doesn’t matter, Musk allies say
item.description: Musk allies spin DOGE as having a "higher purpose" beyond federal budget cuts.

item.title: NJ’s answer to flooding: it has bought out and demolished 1,200 properties
item.description: The state deals with flooding and sea level rise by buying homes in flood prone areas.

item.title: Star that seemed to vanish more than 130 years ago is found again
item.description: In 1892, astronomer Edward Emerson Barnard thought he saw a bright star near Venus, but then it vanished. We may now know why

item.title: Stranger Things series finale trailer is here
item.description: Netflix's finale will also have a two-day theatrical release to more than 600 locations.

item.title: NASA's Chandra rings in the new year with the Champagne Cluster
item.description: Celebrate the New Year with the "Champagne Cluster," a galaxy cluster seen in this new image from NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory and optical telescopes.

item.title: Physicists stirred up controversy with scientific cooking tips in 2025
item.description: Cacio e pepe pasta and boiled eggs were the subjects of meticulous studies aiming to help cooks achieve perfection, but the reimagined recipes weren't always well-received

item.title: Most sensitive radio observations to date find no evidence of technosignature from 3I/ATLAS
item.description: Since the interstellar object (ISO) 3I/ATLAS was first discovered on July 1, 2025, it has garnered much attention, including speculation, hopes and fears that it may somehow contain evidence of technologically advanced civilizations outside of our solar system.

item.title: French ban on 'forever chemicals' in cosmetics, clothing to enter force
item.description: A French ban on the production and sale of cosmetics and most clothing containing polluting and health-threatening "forever chemicals" goes into force on Thursday.

item.title: The year's first meteor shower and supermoon clash in January skies
item.description: The year's first supermoon and meteor shower will sync up in January skies, but the light from one may dim the other.

item.title: The century-long hunt for the gigantic meteorite that vanished
item.description: A soldier returned from the Sahara desert in 1916 with a wild story about a meteorite that dwarfed all others. Over 100 years of hunting yielded nothing – but now twin brothers think they have solved the puzzle

item.title: Image: JWST captures colliding spiral galaxies
item.description: Mid-infrared observations from NASA's James Webb Space Telescope, shown in white, gray, and red, are combined here with X-ray data from NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory, highlighted in blue. Together, these different wavelengths reveal a detailed and layered view of a pair of colliding spiral galaxies, captured in an image released on Dec. 1, 2025.

item.title: West Coast levee failures show growing risks from America's aging flood defenses
item.description: In recent weeks, powerful atmospheric river storms have swept across Washington, Oregon and California, unloading enormous amounts of rain. As rivers surged, they overtopped or breached multiple levees—those long, often unnoticed barriers holding floodwaters back from homes and towns.

item.title: Clouds are vital to life—but many are becoming wispy ghosts. Here's how to see the changes above us
item.description: As a scholar researching clouds, I have spent much of my time trying to understand the economy of the sky. Not the weather reports showing scudding rainclouds, but the deeper logic of cloud movements, their distributions and densities and the way they intervene in light, regulate temperatures and choreograph heat flows across our restless planet.

item.title: Looking for friends, lobsters may stumble into an ecological trap
item.description: Gathering for mutual defense puts young spiny lobsters at risk of predators.

item.title: New dataset maps global city boundaries in high resolution from 2000 to 2022
item.description: A research team led by Prof. Liu Liangyun from the Aerospace Information Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (AIRCAS) has produced the first comprehensive, high-resolution map of global city and town boundaries, offering a view of how urban boundaries have expanded and transformed over the past two decades. The new dataset—derived from 30-meter-resolution satellite observations—fills a long-standing gap in global urban studies.

item.title: The cassette tape made a comeback in 2025 thanks to a DNA upgrade
item.description: With a storage capacity of 36 petabytes, a DNA-based cassette tape can hold every song every recorded, and it could be on the market within five years

item.title: ASKAP discovers a spectacular outflow in a nearby galaxy
item.description: Using the Australian Square Kilometer Array Pathfinder (ASKAP), an international team of astronomers has discovered a spectacular bipolar outflow from the disk of a nearby galaxy known as ESO 130-G012. The finding was reported in a paper published December 17 on the pre-print server arXiv.

item.title: What's inside Mexico's Popocatépetl volcano? Scientists obtain first 3D images
item.description: In the predawn darkness, a team of scientists climbs the slope of Mexico's Popocatépetl volcano, one of the world's most active and whose eruption could affect millions of people. Its mission: figure out what is happening under the crater.

item.title: 2025 was one of three hottest years on record, scientists say
item.description: Climate change worsened by human behavior made 2025 one of the three hottest years on record, scientists said.

item.title: Climate policies can backfire by eroding 'green' values, study finds
item.description: A popular vision of life after climate action looks like vegetarians riding bikes, city centers without cars, and people foregoing air travel. But a new paper published in Nature Sustainability finds that climate policies targeting lifestyle changes (say, urban car bans) actually may weaken people's green values, thereby undermining support for other needed environmental policies.

item.title: A controversial experiment threatened to kill the multiverse in 2025
item.description: A photon was apparently detected in two places at once in a twist on the classic double-slit experiment, but many physicists didn't accept the results
